summary: The translation is close to the Hebrew and keeps the Yerushalmi and the Rambam quotations, the fixed terms and the honorifics. The faults are: the transliterations '(yesh me-ayin)' and '(yesh me-yesh)' that the wave 1 ruling forbids; Exod 20:2-3 given with 'before Me' that the author does not quote; the Rambam quotation closed wrongly around the author's link; 'Epicureans', 'Beriah' and 'Chavat Yair' against the decisions; Gen 1:2 unrecognised in the Ravad; הרב dropped before Lechem Mishneh; and the long sentence at 2:11.191-232, whose subject 'three or four words' was misread, with שם glossed 'any' or 'a' in the Rambam's list. Three decisions questions are raised.

patches.value: In the Yerushalmi, Shabbat, chapter Bemah Ishah, our Sages of blessed memory said: "'And the appearance of the fourth is like a son of the gods.' Rabbi Reuven said: At that hour an angel came down and slapped that wicked one on his mouth, and said to him: 'Is your word right, and is there a son for him?' He returned and said: 'Blessed be the God of Shadrach, Meishach and Abed-nego, who sent His angel and saved His servants.' 'His son' is not written here, but 'His angel.' Thus far." That is to say, Nebuchadnezzar the wicked thought that the angels are effects, descending in a chain of descent from him by nature, like a son from the father, according to the words of the Kabbalists concerning the sefirot of all the worlds, and likewise the souls; and for this the angel slapped him. And he returned and said: 'who sent His angel, etc.' Here you have it explicit, coming out of the words of Midrash Rabbah and the Yerushalmi, contrary to the words of the Kabbalists. And all that exists, the Holy One, blessed be He, brought into being in His kindness, something from nothing, from the first form down to a small gnat; and not that they are drawn from His essence, as the son comes into being by the power of the seed drawn from his father.
patches.reason: Decisions (Rulings from wave 1): יש מאין is translated, 'something from nothing', with no transliteration; the parenthesis '(yesh me-ayin)' is removed. Also: 'his angel' takes the capital like 'His son' and 'His angel' in the same quotation; 'הרי לך מפורש יוצא … היפך' keeps לך ('you have it') and has no added 'that this is'.

patches.value: יש מאין: 'something from nothing' (creation ex nihilo). The phrase is translated, not transliterated (decisions, wave 1: יש מאין / יש מיש).
patches.reason: The old note said decisions.md has no fixed form; it has one.

patches.value: אלההון: Aramaic 'their God'. The suffix is redundant before 'די שדרך מישך ועביד נגו' ('of Shadrach, Meshach and Abed-nego'), so Dan 3:28 is read 'the God of Shadrach …'; the English does the same.
patches.reason: A learner meets 'their' in the gloss and not in the English; the note explains the idiom.

patches.value: ושכל: the ש is 'that'. It continues the previous sentence ('here you have it explicit … and that all that exists …'); the English starts a new sentence because the Hebrew has a full stop. PROPOSED RULING: keep the full stop and the main clause; the note records that the ש is a complementizer ('and that all').
patches.reason: DECISIONS GAP: the checklist (a full stop in the Hebrew is a full stop in the English, every sentence has a main clause) does not cover a sentence that opens with 'and that'. Proposed: keep as translated, with this note.

value: The Yerushalmi is quoted as the author's source, and its Aramaic is translated as he gives it. Dan 3:25 and 3:28 are quoted inside it, in single quotation marks.
'ע"כ' (2:10.53) closes the Yerushalmi quotation. From 2:10.54 the author argues in his own voice, and his argument turns on the words 'בר' (son) and 'מלאכיה' (his angel).
'ובר אית ליה?' is an Aramaic question, 'and is there a son for him?'. 'סטרו' (2:10.21, 2:10.76) is a verb of the angel's action, 'slapped him'.

'ולא שהם נמשכים' (2:10.107-109) is 'and not that they are drawn': the negative ולא rejects the Kabbalists' claim that the angels and all things are drawn from His essence like a son from the seed. 'ושכל' (2:10.95) opens with ש, 'that'.
patches.reason: The old fourth note called שהם נמשכים 'a negation'; the negation is ולא.

value: Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, had Shadrach, Meishach and Abed-nego thrown into a furnace (Dan 3), and called the fourth figure he saw there 'like a son of the gods' (Dan 3:25). In the Yerushalmi's story an angel strikes him for it. The author quotes it against the Kabbalists' claim that the angels descend from God as a son from a father.
patches.reason: The old note said the author quotes the story 'to show that the angel is not the son of a god'; the story and the author's use of it are now stated separately.

patches.value: The conclusion from all this is that no face or form is to be worshipped of all the created things that exist in the upper and the lower world, which the Name, may He be blessed, brought into being in His kindness. For to Him alone it is fitting to worship and to pray, and for this the commandment and the warning came at Sinai: "I am the LORD your God. You shall have no other gods," as the Rambam of blessed memory wrote in chapter two of the Laws of Idolatry. And in chapter three of the Laws of Repentance he wrote, and these are his words: "And these are those who have no share in the world to come, but are cut off and perish for the greatness of their wickedness and their sins, forever and ever: the heretics and the apikorsim, etc." And in the law that follows it he wrote: "Five are those that are called heretics. The one who says that there is no God, and no ruler of the world, and the one who says that there is a ruler, but they are two or more, and the one who says that there is one Lord, but He is a body and possessed of a form, and the one who says that He is not alone the first and the rock of all. Likewise one who worships one other than Him in order to be an intercessor between him and the Lord of the worlds. Each of these five is a heretic. Thus far." And the Rav Lechem Mishneh wrote on the fourth division that our Master wrote, "and the one who says that He is not alone the first, etc." The Ravad wrote: "like one who said, your God is a great painter, but He found for Himself great pigments, formlessness and void, and darkness and water and wind, and with them made what He made." Thus far, the words of the Ravad. And the Rav Lechem Mishneh explains that his intention is to add to the words of our Master that although he concedes that no cause preceded our God, for whose sake He came to be, but says that He created the world something from something, then this one is a heretic; see there. In our case, the belief of the new Kabbalah, as explained in their books, according to our understanding and the understanding of many great ones, wise of heart, among our Rabbis who separated from it, early and late, like the Ribash and Chavot Yair, cited in Pitchei Teshuvah and the other later authorities: in it have gathered and come three or four of these words that our Rabbis said, that whoever believes thus has no share in the world to come. First, a multiplicity of divinities: Ein Sof, and Adam Kadma'ah, and Adam Kadmon, and Atik, and Arikh Anpin, and Abba and Imma, and Ze'ir and his Nukva! Second, that they have a subtle body, namely light, and Ein Sof is a soul to these bodies. Third, that the worship is not to the First Cause, which they call Ein Sof, but to Ze'ir Anpin, which is the last cause among these causes. Fourth, that he is an intermediary drawing down the flow from those upper attributes, which are Atik, Arikh Anpin, Abba and Imma, and they call him son of Abba and Imma, and he is also father to the Keter of Creation, according to the chain of descent of the worlds, in their opinion, the Merciful One save us.
patches.reason: (1) Exod 20:2-3: the author quotes 'אנכי ה' אלהיך לא יהיה לך אלהים אחרים' with nothing omitted by mark; 'before Me' (על פני) is not on the page and the ellipsis is not in the Hebrew (Quotations: translate only what is on the page; Lev 19:4 ruling). The Hebrew has a comma after אחרים, so the sentence goes on: '… gods,' as the Rambam … wrote'; 'and in chapter three' opens a new sentence ('And'). (2) The Rambam's words stop at וכו'; 'ובדין שאחריו כ'' is the author's link, so the quotation marks close after 'etc.' and open again at 'Five'. The LM's quotation of the Rambam takes double marks (explicit quotation). (3) האפיקורסין: 'apikorsim' (ruling: אפיקורוס → 'apikoros'), not 'Epicureans'. (4) הרב לחם משנה / הרב לח"מ: הרב is a word of the Hebrew and was dropped; see the question at token 2:11.127. (5) תהו ובהו in the Ravad's list is Gen 1:2 and is translated ('formlessness and void'), not transliterated. (6) יש מיש: 'something from something', no transliteration (ruling). (7) 'נקבצו באו בה': the subject is 'תלת וארבע מלי' ('three or four words'), plural like the verbs, and בה is 'in it'; the old English had 'gathered and came against it' with the subject of the verbs left out and 'three or four of these words' hanging; 'דאמור רבנן, דהמאמין כן …' is indirect speech, no quotation marks. (8) Chavot Yair is the fixed spelling in the decisions. (9) אמצעי has no article: 'an intermediary'. (10) דבריאה: the four worlds are translated (Emanation, Creation, Formation, Making): 'of Creation'. (11) לזולתו: 'one other than Him'. (12) Pronouns for God take the capital as in 2:10 and as in the Lechem Mishneh's own quotation of the same Rambam clause ('He is not alone the first' at 2:11.105 and 2:11.136).

patches.value: Exod 20:2-3 is cut short by the author after 'אחרים': the English gives only what is written (no 'who brought you out …', no 'before Me'). See `apparatus`.
patches.reason: DECISIONS GAP: the fixed rendering of Exod 20:2-3 ('I am the LORD your God … You shall have no other gods before Me.') is for the verse as quoted in full; the Quotations rule says to translate only what is on the page. Proposed ruling: the fixed rendering applies only where the author quotes על פני; a cut quotation takes the same wording up to where he stops, without the ellipsis.

value: The Rambam's words run from 2:11.51 ('וז"ל') to 2:11.125 ('ע"כ'). They are cut short at 'וכו'' (2:11.70); 'ובדין שאחריו כ'' (2:11.71-73) is the author's link, so the quotation marks close and open again around it. The author's gloss starts at 2:11.126.
'כ'' (2:11.73, 2:11.140) is 'wrote', an abbreviation of כתב; 'שכ'' (2:11.39) is 'that wrote'. 'הרב' (2:11.127, 2:11.165) is a word of the text, 'the Rav', before the book's name.
'שאין לעבוד' (2:11.4-5) is 'that one must not worship': 'לעבוד' is the verb 'to worship', used of God throughout the paragraph.
'שם' in 'שאין שם אלוה' (2:11.79-81), 'שיש שם מנהיג' (2:11.86-88) and 'שיש שם רבון' (2:11.95-97) is the adverb 'there' of the existential 'there is', not 'name'.

In the long sentence at 2:11.191-232 the subject of 'נקבצו באו' (2:11.218-219) is 'תלת וארבע מלי' (2:11.221-223), 'three or four words'; 'בה' is 'in it', the belief of the new Kabbalah. The words between ('כפי המבואר … ושאר אחרונים') say by whose understanding. 'דאמור רבנן' is Aramaic: 'that the Rabbis said'.
'חדא', 'שנית', 'שלישית', 'רביעית' (2:11.233, 248, 259, 275) number the four 'words'. The first is a noun phrase (רבוי האלוהות); the others open with שהם, שהעבודה, שהוא.
patches.reason: The old fourth note said every item is followed by שהם or שהעבודה (the first has neither, the fourth has שהוא); the old notes lacked the point about שם and about the subject of נקבצו באו; the old note at 2:11.4-5 stays.

patches.value: The paragraph is the author's conclusion from the Rambam's law (the Rambam, the Lechem Mishneh and the Ravad are quoted), followed by the four 'words' of the Rabbis that he finds in the new Kabbalah.
patches.reason: The old note put the four objections in the words of the Lechem Mishneh and the Ravad; they are the author's own.

value: Exod 20:2-3: the author quotes 'אנכי ה' אלהיך לא יהיה לך אלהים אחרים', leaving out 'who brought you out of the land of Egypt …' (v. 2) and 'על פני' (v. 3); the English follows his wording, without 'before Me'.
Rambam, Laws of Idolatry ch. 2 and Laws of Repentance ch. 3 (Mishneh Torah), as the author gives them; no halakhah number is added. The Rambam's quotation is cut short at 'וכו'' (2:11.70).

Gen 1:2: 'תהו ובהו וחשך ומים ורוח' in the Ravad's words echoes the verse ('formless and void, and darkness … and the wind (or spirit) of God … the waters'); here the words are the painter's materials, so 'formlessness and void' and 'wind'.
The Lechem Mishneh and the Ravad are quoted as the author gives them; 'וכו'' is kept as 'etc.'.
יש מיש: 'something from something', translated, not transliterated (decisions, wave 1: יש מאין / יש מיש).
חו"י: the expansion Chavot Yair (the fixed spelling in the decisions) is a reading, not a certainty.
שם (2:11.80, 87, 96) is 'there'; 'name' is not possible in the grammar of 'שיש שם'.
patches.reason: The old lines said the English gives 'before Me' by the decisions and a transliterated יש מיש 'because decisions are silent'; both are wrong (see the english patch). Gen 1:2 is added; Chavot Yair, the Rambam's cut and שם are recorded.

value: The Mishneh Torah is the Rambam's code of Jewish law; the Laws of Idolatry and the Laws of Repentance are two of its sections, as cited here.
The Lechem Mishneh is a commentary on the Mishneh Torah. Pitchei Teshuvah is a commentary on the Shulchan Arukh.
patches.reason: The Laws of Idolatry and Repentance are sections of the code, not 'books'.

value.english: the authorities gathered and came against it: three or four of these words that our Rabbis said, "Whoever believes thus has no share in the world to come."
value.note: The reading of the draft, which makes the Ribash, Chavot Yair and the later authorities the subject and בה 'against it'; the English chosen takes 'three or four words' as the subject and בה as 'in it'.

patches.reason: A real alternative parse of the Hebrew (plural verbs agree with either subject); the grammar allows it.
